name: prover9
desc: Automated theorem prover for first-order and equational logic
why: An automated theorem prover from the McCune lineage that can actually prove equational theorems you feed it.

brief.what_it_is: Prover9 is an automated theorem prover for first-order and equational logic, and Mace4 is its companion that searches for finite models and counterexamples. You give it logic formulas as input, and it tries to derive a proof of the stated theorem using resolution and paramodulation. The LADR-2026 revision, per the site, accepts native TPTP input and emits TSTP proof output. The installed executables are prover9 and mace4.
brief.why_it_exists: The site presents Prover9 as the successor to the Otter prover, and says its purpose is to support students, educators, and researchers in first-order and equational reasoning. The 2026 maintainers describe the work as a modernization of William McCune's codebase that stays faithful to his documented intentions.
brief.how_it_works: Prover9 uses resolution and paramodulation, which is the mechanism that lets it reason about equality, to search for a derivation of the goal from the given axioms. Mace4 instead searches for finite models, and a model it finds can serve as a counterexample to a conjecture. The homepage also mentions a portfolio strategy selector trained on 32 problem features that picks a search strategy, but it gives no detail on how that works.
brief.install_notes: Homepage download section lists macOS and Linux and says 'See GitHub for details' for the latest release. The GitHub repository is referenced but its URL was not given in the fetched text, so I did not follow it. The homepage says existing Prover9 and Mace4 input files run unchanged under LADR-2026, and that LADR-2026 is recommended over the 2009 version. I did not see configuration or first-run steps.
brief.standout: Prover9 is the rare prover that handles equational theorems through paramodulation, not just pure first-order clauses. The 2026 revision adds native TPTP input and TSTP output, so its proofs can be checked by external verifiers such as GDV and Ivy, according to the site.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage has an update dated 2026-mar-17, and a 'What's New' entry lists LADR-2026-8A from Mar 2026. The site names two maintainers, Jeffrey P. Machado and Larry Lesyna. The McCune-era page at cs.unm.edu is still up, marked as the older version.
brief.caveats: Performance and benchmark claims (1.00-rated TPTP problems, 5-10 percent speedup, the portfolio selector) are the project's own statements and I did not verify them. The download section lists only macOS and Linux. The license is GPLv2, per the homepage. I did not check the GitHub repository, so build requirements and install details beyond the homepage are unknown.
quotes: Prover9 is an automated theorem prover for first-order and equational logic, and Mace4 searches for finite models and counterexamples.
Your existing input files run without modification.
The theorem prover and finite model finder you already know, now with a hardened engine, native TPTP input, TSTP output, and capacity for greater than 100,000 formulas.
